title: Reheating Physics After Inflation
bottleneck: The epoch connecting inflation's end to the hot Big Bang — reheating — is almost entirely unconstrained: its temperature could be anywhere from MeV to 10^15 GeV, and its dynamics (parametric resonance, inflaton couplings) are model-dependent. Reheating uncertainties propagate into predictions for N_eff, dark matter production, and gravitational-wave backgrounds. If reheating is prolonged, it alters the mapping between CMB scales and inflationary e-folds, shifting inferred model parameters.
why_it_blocks: Every inflationary prediction carries a hidden reheating asterisk, limiting how precisely cosmology can test the early universe.
current_state: Only indirect bounds exist (BBN requires reheating above ~MeV); no probe of the reheating era is currently feasible. Constraints from the effective number of relativistic species and primordial black hole bounds provide only weak, indirect limits.

sources.title: The Measure Problem in Eternal Inflation (arXiv:1801.05016)
